name: IN/OUT: Breathing Timer
subtitle: Breathe for what's next
shortDescription: Guided breathing, custom patterns and private before-and-after check-ins.
description:
Make room for a reset with IN/OUT. Choose a breathing practice, follow the visual guide, and notice how you feel afterward.

PRACTICE YOUR WAY
Explore nine built-in protocols, including Physiological Sigh, Box Breathing, Coherent Breathing, Extended Exhale and Equal Breathing. Follow concise voice or sound cues, optional haptics, and protocol-specific visual guides.

BUILD A ROUTINE
Create your own ordered phases, adjust durations and cycles, or chain protocols in Mix Mode. Save, edit, duplicate and delete routines on your phone.

NOTICE YOUR STATE SHIFT
Optionally rate your tension before and after a session. See your own reported change, review history and explore your practice over time. State Shift is self-reported, not a biometric measurement.

OFFLINE AND ACCOUNT-FREE
Core breathing, custom routines and history work offline. No account, subscription or advertising is required. Sessions pause when you switch apps or lock your phone and can recover from the last saved checkpoint after a restart.

BREATHE COMFORTABLY
Stop if you feel dizzy, faint or unwell. Never practice while driving, operating machinery, swimming, bathing or near water. IN/OUT is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any medical condition. Consult a healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
reviewNotes: No account or login is needed. Start on Today, choose Start reset, choose or skip the pre-rating, and complete the 48-second Physiological Sigh. Then answer or skip the post-rating and view History. Audio follows system volume and the iPhone silent switch. App switching and locking intentionally pause sessions; resume manually. Custom contains saved pattern and mix editors. Settings contains privacy, safety, support, and local deletion controls. All nine released protocols and custom routines are free. There are no purchases, ads, health sensors, or medical diagnoses. High-intensity cyclic breathing is excluded.
